Rugby.title: Canada and USA Enter High Performance Agreement
Rugby.summary: Canada and USA Enter High Performance Agreement Americas Rugby News
Rugby.copy:
Rugby Canada and USA Rugby have launched a four-year high-performance pathway agreement to unify player development and lock in a recurring annual calendar of cross-border competition. Rather than treating one another solely as fierce regional rivals, the two governing bodies are combining resources to build a shared ecosystem of senior test matches, joint training camps, and age-grade tournaments. This alliance establishes a predictable, long-term foundation designed to elevate North American rugby on the world stage over the next decade.

The four-year high-performance pathway agreement between USA Rugby and Rugby Canada builds upon one of North America’s longest-running sporting rivalries. Dating back to the first men’s test match in 1977 and the historic first women’s test outside of Europe in 1987, the two nations have frequently clashed across regional tournaments like the Churchill Cup, the Americas Rugby Championship, and the Pacific Nations Cup. While cross-border youth tours and joint developmental programming were a regular staple of North American rugby prior to 2020, those collaborative pathways were largely neglected in the post-COVID era. As a result, the rival unions often relied on sporadic, ad-hoc fixtures rather than a unified approach to player progression.

Rugby.title: PREM clubs on alert as Top 14 consider salary cap rule change
Rugby.summary: French clubs could be set to gain another major advantage in the transfer market, with the Ligue Nationale de Rugby (LNR) set to vote early next year on plans to allow Top 14 clubs to exclude one player from their salary cap.
bullets: The Ligue Nationale de Rugby (LNR) will vote on 10 February on plans to let Top 14 clubs exclude one player from their salary cap. The base Top 14 cap has risen from €10.7m (£8.92m) to €11.1m (£9.2m), with limits on international player allowances, and the change could take effect as early as next season.

The Top 14 cap remains well above the Gallagher PREM's £6.4m per squad, which can stretch to £7.8m with credits. PREM clubs must spend a baseline £5.4m and may have one marquee player outside the cap, but talks on a second have stalled because seven of ten clubs must agree. In France, Toulouse and Montpellier want up to three exempt players, Clermont and Bayonne are said to be opposed, and a proposed €500,000 limit on the marquee player is a stumbling block.
Rugby.copy:

Rugby.title: Dupont picked at 10 amid France fly-half crisis
Rugby.summary: France will take on world champions South Africa on Friday with captain Antoine Dupont filling in at fly-half because of a raft of injuries.
bullets: France captain Antoine Dupont will start at fly-half for Friday's Nations Championship game against world champions South Africa in Paris, because Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy are unavailable. Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, who won Olympic sevens gold alongside Dupont in 2024, will win his fourth cap on the wing.

Maxime Lucu had been expected to play at 10, having replaced Ntamack, who injured a shoulder 32 minutes into Saturday's 54-17 win over Fiji. Coach Fabien Galthie chose Dupont, who filled in at fly-half for Toulouse in 2023-24, and picked Julien Marchand and Gregory Alldritt to counter the Springboks' forward power. South Africa have won nine of their past 10 Tests against France and made one change, with Wilco Louw replacing Thomas du Toit.
Rugby.copy:
France captain Antoine Dupont will fill in at fly-half for Friday's Nations Championship game against world champions South Africa in Paris. Grandidier-Nkanang focused on Sevens, winning Olympic gold alongside Dupont in 2024 before making a successful switch back to the 15-a-side game with Pau. Dupont, a specialist scrum-half with only a handful of appearances at 10, has been forced into fly-half by the absence of Matthieu Jalibert, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy.

He will meet a surgeon on Thursday to review scans before a recovery plan is devised.

Baxter said the balance of opinion is that Feyi-Waboso is unlikely to need an operation, with a high ankle sprain meaning a minimum of four to six weeks. Exeter's back three has been hit by injuries: Campbell Ridl is out for most of the campaign with a knee ligament injury, Tommy Wyatt is a month from fitness, and Paul Brown-Bampoe returned against Bath after heel surgery. Dallas McLeod has joined from New Zealand.

Rugby.title: England and South Africa confirm 2035 Rugby World Cup hosting decisions
Rugby.summary: England and South Africa confirm 2035 Rugby World Cup hosting decisions Ruck.co.uk
bullets: England and South Africa will not host the 2035 Rugby World Cup after neither nation submitted a bid before the application deadline. Both former hosts had been linked with the tournament, leaving Spain, Japan and a South American consortium of Argentina, Uruguay, Chile and Brazil in contention. SA Rugby president Mark Alexander said South Africa would not bid because of the cost of upgrading its stadiums.

World Rugby is expected to identify its preferred host in May 2027, with the final decision scheduled for November. Australia will host the 2027 tournament, followed by the United States in 2031. England last staged the men's event in 2015, while South Africa last hosted in 1995 and is also exploring a potential Olympic Games bid.
Rugby.copy:
England and South Africa will not host the 2035 Rugby World Cup after neither nation submitted a bid before the application deadline. Both former hosts had been linked with staging the tournament, but neither entered the race, leaving three rival projects competing for rugby's biggest event.

Spain, Japan and a South American consortium are now in contention, with World Rugby set to make its final decision next year. South Africa last hosted the tournament in 1995, when Nelson Mandela famously presented François Pienaar with the Webb Ellis Cup.

Rugby.title: Uganda win Rugby Africa Women’s Sevens championship to qualify for SVNS 3
Rugby.summary: Uganda win Rugby Africa Women’s Sevens championship to qualify for SVNS 3 Rugbypass.com
bullets: Uganda won the Rugby Africa Women's Sevens championship in Nairobi, claiming the continental title for the first time and qualifying as Africa's representative at HSBC SVNS 3 in Dubai on 28-29 November 2026. They beat hosts Kenya 19-14 in the semi-final, with Peace Lekuru scoring the winning try on the final play, then defeated Tunisia 33-0 in the final.

Kenya, who had beaten Uganda 22-5 in the Safari Sevens last month and won Youth Olympics gold in Dakar, took bronze with a 27-7 win over Zimbabwe. Head coach Simon Odongo said the margins in sevens are small and the team will return stronger in 2027. Tunisia recorded their best finish since 2013, while South Africa Women's 'A' side finished sixth after losing 17-12 to Zambia.
Rugby.copy:
Uganda have fired a massive warning shot to the rest of Africa’s rugby nations, getting the last laugh in 2026 to claim the Rugby Africa Women’s Sevens championship and qualify as the continent’s representative at the HSBC SVNS 3 tournament, set to take place in Dubai in a fortnight.

The Lady Cranes came into the weekend’s competition at the RFUEA Grounds in Nairobi, Kenya, with stiff competition, coming up against the likes of rapidly improving sides Tunisia, Zimbabwe and Zambia, as well the South Africa Women’s ‘A’ side, and the strong favourites for the weekend, the Kenya Lionesses.

Rugby.title: Borthwick gets a glimpse of first-choice back three – before injuries strike again
Rugby.summary: Borthwick gets a glimpse of first-choice back three – before injuries strike again The Guardian
Rugby.copy:
Rugby, at its heart, is a simple game. Win the collisions and you’ll more than likely win the match. Rule the skies, own the floor and the chances are you’ll end up on the right side of the ledger. Put square pegs in square holes and you can achieve the sort of attacking fluidity required for a record score against Australia. The complicated bit, once you stop trying to put them in round holes, is keeping those square pegs fit.

England’s emphatic win against the Wallabies on Sunday was the first time in two years Borthwick has been able to field a back three of Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman and George Furbank. It was also the first time they have lined up with 11, 14 and 15 on their respective backs.

Rugby.title: England wing Feyi-Waboso out of Nations Championship
Rugby.summary: England wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is ruled out of the rest of the Nations Championship as his injury misfortune continues.
bullets: England wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has been ruled out of the rest of the Nations Championship after injuring his ankle in the 32nd minute of the 45-22 win over Australia. The injury came in a hip-drop tackle by Angus Bell, who received a yellow card, and Henry Pollock replaced him after half-time. The 23-year-old missed the 2025 Six Nations after shoulder surgery and this year's edition with a hamstring injury.

Seb Atkinson, Ollie Chessum and George Furbank are also out of Saturday's match against Japan, and flanker Tom Curry will miss the autumn with hip discomfort. Max Hicks and Jack Kenningham have been called into the 36-man squad. England then face New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday 21 November, with finals weekend on 27-29 November.

The 23-year-old injured his ankle in the first half of Sunday's 45-22 win over Australia in a "hip-drop" tackle by Angus Bell, for which the Wallabies prop received a yellow card.

England will also be without a handful of other key players for the match against Japan on Saturday, with Seb Atkinson, forward Ollie Chessum and full-back George Furbank all ruled out.

Rugby.title: Argentina's Cruz Mallia facing months on sidelines as history repeats itself
Rugby.summary: Argentina and Toulouse utility back Juan Cruz Mallia is facing a potentially lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering a fresh injury to his right knee during the Pumas' defeat to Ireland in Dublin.
bullets: Argentina and Toulouse utility back Juan Cruz Mallia faces a potentially lengthy absence after a fresh injury to his right knee during the Pumas' defeat to Ireland in Dublin on Friday night. The 30-year-old, who underwent surgery less than a year ago for an anterior cruciate ligament rupture, was hit late by Ireland lock James Ryan. According to Le Figaro, he has returned to Toulouse for further medical examinations.

He had previously ruptured his ACL after a late tackle by Tom Curry in a 27-23 loss to England in the 2025 Autumn Nations Series. Toulouse's injury list is growing, with France's Romain Ntamack expected to be out until the New Year after dislocating his shoulder against Fiji. No timeframe has been set for Mallia's recovery, but reports in France suggest Toulouse could bring in a medical joker if the injury proves serious.
Rugby.copy:
Argentina and Toulouse utility back Juan Cruz Mallia is facing a potentially lengthy spell on the sidelines after suffering a fresh injury to his right knee during the Pumas’ defeat to Ireland in Dublin.

The 30-year-old was forced off during Friday night’s Nations Championship encounter, sparking fears that he may have damaged the same knee on which he underwent surgery less than a year ago following an anterior cruciate ligament rupture.

Rugby.title: Ireland's Jansen ruled out of Fiji and Bok games
Rugby.summary: Sean Jansen is ruled out of the remainder of Ireland's Nations Championship campaign with a knee injury, further depleting head coach Andy Farrell's options at number eight.
bullets: Ireland number eight Sean Jansen has been ruled out of the rest of the Nations Championship campaign with a knee injury sustained during Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina in Dublin. He will return to Connacht for rehabilitation, further depleting head coach Andy Farrell's back-row options with Caelan Doris and Jack Conan already injured. Uncapped Ulster forward David McCann has been called up.

Hooker Dan Sheehan, squad captain in Doris' absence, will miss Saturday's home match with Fiji (20:10 GMT) after a concussion and is a doubt for the South Africa game on 21 November because of 12-day return-to-play protocols. The coaching staff are hopeful wing Rob Baloucoune (cramp) and flanker Josh van der Flier (ankle) will be available, while centre Bundee Aki is expected to resume full training on Tuesday. Gus McCarthy has joined the squad at hooker, and Ireland then travel to Twickenham for a finals weekend fixture.

Rugby.title: New World Rugby rankings announced as global game split into three tiers
Rugby.summary: New World Rugby rankings announced as global game split into three tiers Wales Online
bullets: The first round of the Nations Championship autumn leg has shaped the World Rugby rankings, with South Africa remaining number one after a 66-7 win over Italy in Rome. New Zealand beat Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield, and Ireland, the third-ranked side, beat Argentina 42-12. England's 45-22 win over Australia produced the biggest rankings gain, 1.31 points, taking them close to fourth-placed France, who beat Fiji.

Wales' 28-21 win over Japan moved them further ahead of Italy and Japan and within 0.42 ranking points of ninth-placed Fiji. Next weekend, France host South Africa, Wales play New Zealand, England face Japan, Ireland meet Fiji, Scotland play Australia and Italy host Argentina. Wales' fixture against seventh-placed Australia is viewed as a target for breaking into the top eight.
Rugby.copy:
The first round of the Nations Championship's autumn leg has reaffirmed the huge divide that currently exists in the world game. South Africa's 66-7 demolition of Italy in Rome underlined their status as the world's number one side, showing the gulf in class between the elite and teams further down the pecking order.

Likewise, New Zealand's comfortable 43-21 win over Scotland at Murrayfield proved the two southern hemisphere giants remain a level above the challenging pack in the second tier of teams between fifth and eighth in the rankings table.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock powers seven-try England to crushing victory against Australia
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock powers seven-try England to crushing victory against Australia The Guardian
bullets: England beat Australia with seven tries in their Nations Championship match, scoring a record number of points against the Wallabies. Henry Pollock scored two tries after replacing Manny Feyi-Waboso on the wing at half-time, with others from Jamie George, Ollie Chessum, Joe Heyes, Jack van Poortvliet and Ben Spencer. Australia's tries came from Max Jorgensen, Filipo Daugunu and Jeremy Williams.

Angus Bell was shown a yellow card for an illegal tackle on Feyi-Waboso, who was later seen in a medical boot, and England scored soon after. They face Japan and New Zealand over the next two Saturdays and could still reach the Nations Championship final at home at the end of the month. The result follows a Six Nations campaign that put Steve Borthwick's regime under pressure.
Rugby.copy:
England had promised to do their talking on the field and so it came to pass. After a turbulent few days, this result was certainly a thumping riposte to newspaper reports that all is not well within the court of Steve Borthwick. If Australia had imagined they might encounter distracted, half-hearted hosts, this seven-try romp suggested the precise opposite.

Maybe Borthwick should commission the Times to write his motivational pre-match speeches every week. On this evidence the Wallabies have some massive issues to address but, equally, England were comfortably the better, more energetic side. Further improvement will still be demanded, of course, but this record number of points against Australia was easily their most satisfying all-round outing of the calendar year to date. Their three defining Ds – defence, discipline and desire – were conspicuous throughout and, at long last, they are starting to trust their exciting attacking talent out wide.

bullets: Eben Etzebeth has been recalled to the Springboks squad for the Nations Championship after uncapped fly-half Yaqeen Ahmed, 20, withdrew from the touring party with a shoulder problem. The 147-Test lock had originally been ruled out through injury but has recovered sufficiently to rejoin the group, and is expected to link up with the squad in France on Monday.

Rugby.summary: Ex-WRU chief suggests radical idea for four Welsh clubs amid Anglo-Welsh talks Wales Online
bullets: The Welsh Rugby Union has sent a formal letter to the Rugby Football Union seeking to enter Welsh teams into the Gallagher PREM when it expands from 10 to 12 teams. The RFU says it remains committed to English expansion, while the United Rugby Championship has threatened Wales with legal action.

Former WRU chair Gareth Davies has suggested two Welsh teams could play in the Premiership while two remain in the URC, saying two is the most Wales could get in England. He warned of a cost to enter, including a large payment for league shares, and questioned spending £40m to play in a competition where everyone else loses money. URC chief executive Martin Anayi has appeared committed to four Welsh teams in the URC.
Rugby.copy:
Former Welsh Rugby Union chair Gareth Davies has called for the governing body to split its teams between the Gallagher PREM and United Rugby Championship. The WRU has sent a formal letter to the Rugby Football Union in a bid to enter Welsh teams into the PREM when it expands from 10 to 12 teams. But the RFU currently say they are committed to English expansion, while the URC has threatened Wales with legal action.

That hasn't stopped former WRU chair Davies from believing Welsh rugby could possibly get the best of both worlds. “I think if we can get two teams in the Premiership and maybe two teams carrying on playing in the URC,” Davies told S4C’s Newyddion.

Rugby.title: New Zealand cruise to victory as Scotland fade at Murrayfield
Rugby.summary: New Zealand cruise to victory as Scotland fade at Murrayfield BBC
bullets: New Zealand beat Scotland by seven tries to three at Murrayfield in the Nations Championship, despite a first-half hat-trick from Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman. Wallace Sititi, Ethan de Groot, Codie Taylor, Beauden Barrett (twice), Josh Moorby and Asafo Aumua scored the All Blacks' tries, and only three points separated the sides at half-time.

The All Blacks dominated the second half, scoring 19 unanswered points to lead 43-21 after 50 minutes. Both sides had players sin-binned, with Peter Lakai and Sititi for New Zealand and captain Sione Tuipulotu for Scotland. It was the 34th Test between the nations, with New Zealand now holding 32 wins and two draws since 1905.
Rugby.copy:
Ruthless New Zealand blew Scotland away in a high-class, seven tries to three Nations Championship victory at Murrayfield. Despite a historic first-half hat-trick from Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman, the All Blacks were mostly magnificent, unrelenting and classy. It was the 34th Test between the nations and New Zealand's tally has yet another win - 32 now, with two draws going back to 1905.

Wallace Sititi scored early in a breathless first half. Ashman responded. Ethan de Groot and Codie Taylor hit back to make it 17-7 at the end of the first quarter. New Zealand's Peter Lakai was binned and Ashman got his second while he was off. The sensational Beauden Barrett scored the first of his double straight after. Then, as the bonkerdom stretched on, Sititi was yellow-carded and Ashman made the All Blacks pay with his hat-trick try.

bullets: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has picked Declan Meredith at fly-half for the Nations Championship match against England at Allianz Stadium. Angus Bell returns at loose-head prop, and Len Ikitau comes back in the midfield alongside Isaac Henry.

Ryan Lonergan starts at scrum-half, Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii and Max Jorgensen are on the wings and Tom Wright is at full-back, with Taniela Tupou and Rob Valetini on the bench. Wallabies prop Angus Bell returns after missing the Bledisloe Cup defeats, starting on the loosehead side with Billy Pollard at hooker and Allan Alaalatoa at tighthead. It’s an all-Queensland Reds partnership in the second row, with Josh Canham and Lukhan Salakai-Loto rounding out the tight-five.

Rugby.title: Bok star Faf de Klerk set for extended spell on the sidelines
Rugby.summary: The double World Cup winner suffered an ankle injury in last month's 29-27 defeat to Bayonne in the opening round of the Challenge Cup.
bullets: Faf de Klerk has been ruled out for the rest of the year after the Toyota Cheetahs confirmed an ankle injury sustained in their 29-27 defeat to Bayonne in the opening round of the Challenge Cup on 18 October. The club said the scrum-half will be sidelined for eight weeks and is expected back in early January, in time for Round 3 against Zebre Parma in Italy.

The double World Cup winner, 35, will miss the Cheetahs' debut at their new European home ground, the round two fixture against Dragons at St Helen's in Swansea on 13 December. Marco Jansen van Vuren and Erich Visser will cover at scrum-half. De Klerk helped the Cheetahs reach the Currie Cup semi-finals after his summer move from Japan's Canon Eagles, and won the last of his 60 Springbok caps in July last year.
Rugby.copy:
Faf de Klerk has been ruled out for the remainder of the year after the Toyota Cheetahs issued a medical update on their sidelined Bok star. The double World Cup winner suffered an ankle injury in last month’s 29-27 defeat to Bayonne in the opening round of the Challenge Cup and it has now been confirmed by his club that he won’t play again until January.

In a statement, the Cheetahs said: “Faf de Klerk sustained an ankle injury during the game against Bayonne on 18 October and will be on the sidelines for 8 weeks. He is expected to return in early January, in time for Round 3 of the EPCR Challenge Cup, when the Toyota Cheetahs face Zebre Parma in Italy.

Rugby.title: Fly-half Smith fit to steer England against Wallabies
Rugby.summary: Fly-half Fin Smith recovers from a calf injury and will start for England in their opening Test of the autumn against Australia on Sunday.
bullets: Fly-half Fin Smith has recovered from a calf injury and will start for England against Australia on Sunday in their opening Test of the autumn, a Nations Championship fixture. Smith, 24, had started England's past five matches at 10 but was a doubt after coming off late in Northampton's defeat by Leicester on 24 October. Flanker Ben Curry returns to the Test side after an injury-hit 16 months, with his twin brother Tom ruled out after a training setback.

Exeter back row Greg Fisilau is poised for a first cap on the bench. Alex Coles starts in the second row ahead of George Martin, and Fin Baxter starts at loose-head with Ellis Genge among the replacements. England then face Japan and New Zealand on 14 and 21 November, before a Nations Championship finals weekend play-off. Head coach Steve Borthwick said Australia are a talented side who have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months.
Rugby.copy:
Fly-half Fin Smith has recovered from a calf injury and will start for England in their opening Test of the autumn against Australia on Sunday. Smith has started England's past five matches at 10, but was a doubt to face the Wallabies in the Nations Championship encounter after coming off late on in Northampton's defeat by Leicester on 24 October.

The 24-year-old is joined in the England XV by flanker Ben Curry, who makes his Test return after an injury-hit 16 months. Curry, whose twin brother Tom had an injury setback in training earlier this week that took him out of contention, is seen as key to combating Australia's breakdown specialists Fraser McReight and Carlo Tizzano and ensuring a supply of quick ball to Smith and his backline.

Racket.title: ATP partnership revenues rise 49% to record high
Racket.summary: ATP partnership revenues rise 49% to record high ATP Tour
Racket.copy:
ATP has delivered its strongest partnership performance to date, with central partnership revenues rising 49% year on year in 2026. The increase sees ATP central partnership revenues surpass the $100 million mark for the first time. Since 2022, revenues have increased by more than 200%, driven by new agreements and expanded investment from longstanding partners such as Emirates, Infosys, Nitto, Lexus, Haier and Yokohama, some of which have worked with ATP for more than a decade.

This year’s growth was fuelled by new partnerships with EQT and K-Swiss, alongside continued investment from existing partners. Earlier this week, ATP also announced a multi-year partnership with Julius Baer, which becomes ATP’s first Official Wealth Management Partner and the first Official Partner of the ATP Coaches Programme, with activation across five ATP tournaments on three continents from 2027.

Racket.title: Paralympic medallist Shuker ends 24-year tennis career
Racket.summary: British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker retires after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals.
Racket.copy:
British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker has retired after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals. The 46-year-old represented GB at five consecutive Paralympics and won one silver medal and two bronze between 2012 and 2020, in the women's doubles alongside Jordanne Whiley.

A nine-time Grand Slam finalist and seven-time World Team Cup medalist, Shuker announced during Wimbledon this year that she would retire at the end of the season. At the time she had 98 doubles titles and achieved her aim of reaching 100 earlier this month, when she and Ruby Bishop won at the WC50 Abingdon in Oxfordshire. Shuker also won 39 singles titles.

Racket.title: Lakshya, Srikanth Reach Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 Quarterfinals
Racket.summary: Lakshya, Srikanth Reach Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 Quarterfinals Sportscape Magazine
Racket.copy:
Lakshya Sen beat Dong Tian Yao and Kidambi Srikanth upset World No.8 Kodai Naraoka to reach the Kumamoto Masters Japan 2026 quarterfinals. See the scores. India had a great outing at the Kumamoto Masters 2026 in Japan, with Lakshya Sen and Srikanth Kidambi winning their pre-quarterfinals at the Kumamoto Prefectural Gymnasium. Sen and Kidambi, who recently got promoted in the BWF World Rankings, have now reached the BWF Super 500 quarterfinals. World No.13, Lakshya, beat China’s Dong Tian Yao, 2-0, and World No.31, Kidambi, produced the biggest upset, defeating World No.8, Japan’s Kodai Naraoka, 2-1. The Japan Masters 2026 are an important stepping stone towards the BWF World Tour Finals, which are scheduled in December.

India’s No.1 shuttler in the men’s singles event won against World No.45, Dong, 21-8, 21-14. Sen dominated in both sets, winning the Super 500 quarterfinals. Before Dong, Lakshya won against Chinese Taipei’s Chi Yu Jen, 21-19, 21-18 in 49 minutes. The 25-year-old won the Hylo Open men’s singles title in Germany in October. The win takes the Indian one step closer to the Japan Masters title, which India is yet to win since its beginning in 2023.

Racket.summary: United Cup 2027: GB drawn against France & Australia with Emma Raducanu & Arthur Fery set to star LTA
bullets: Great Britain has been drawn in Group D of the 2027 United Cup, alongside France and host nation Australia. The 10-day event runs from 1-10 January in Perth and Sydney, with 18 nations in six round-robin groups. Group D ties will be played at the Ken Roswell Arena in Sydney from 2-6 January.

Emma Raducanu and British No.1 Arthur Fery lead the GB squad, which also includes Francesca Jones, Jan Choinski, Olivia Nicholls and Neal Skupski. It will be Raducanu's first tournament back after six months out with injury. The top six teams and two best runners-up reach the quarter-finals on 7-8 January, with the final on 10 January. GB has reached the quarter-finals twice since 2023.
Racket.copy:

The 10-day competition will see 18 nations compete across six round-robin groups, with the top six teams and two best-performing runners-up progressing to the quarter-finals. Ties are played as a best-of-three format, including one women’s and one men’s singles match and one mixed doubles rubber.

Racket.title: Emma Raducanu's 202-day tennis absence pays off as comeback confirmed
Racket.summary: Emma Raducanu's 202-day tennis absence pays off as comeback confirmed AOL.co.uk
Racket.copy:
Emma Raducanu has finally confirmed her return to competition at the United Cup after spending months sidelined by a shin injury. The 23-year-old will represent Team GB along with British No. 1 Arthur Fery, and they face France and Australia in the group stages at the beginning of January. Raducanu has not played a match since she lost the Queen's final to Donna Vekic in mid-June. She subsequently pulled out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament and has given little updates on her comeback since.

But Raducanu's lengthy absence has paid off, as she has spent enough time sidelined by injury to get a protected ranking. This is offered to players who have been out for six months, and is based on their ranking before their absence. It can be used to enter up to eight tournaments, including two Grand Slams.

Racket.title: Svitolina comes back from a set down to beat Muchova, moves to 1-1 at FAGE WTA Finals
Racket.summary: Svitolina comes back from a set down to beat Muchova, moves to 1-1 at FAGE WTA Finals WTA Tennis
Racket.copy:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- Just like their past two meetings, Elina Svitolina and Karolina Muchova's second round-robin match at the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals went to a third set. Wednesday, in their third straight meeting to go to a decider, Svitolina edged Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 and will have a chance to compete for a semifinal spot in Friday's group stage finale against [2] Aryna Sabalenka. Muchova falls to 0-2 at the competition, and is eliminated from advancing to the semifinals as a result of Mirra Andreeva's win.

With the comeback, she ended Muchova's impressive 32-0 unbeaten record this season after taking the first set -- 26 of those wins had come in straight sets and six in three sets. Svitolina improves to 19-5 in three sets this season, while Muchova dropped just her third deciding set of 17 this year.

bullets: Mirra Andreeva won 11 games in a row to beat world number two Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 6-0 and reach the semi-finals of the WTA Finals. The French Open champion recovered from 4-1 down in the first set, hitting 16 winners to six unforced errors, while Sabalenka made 23 unforced errors and failed to hit an ace.

Andreeva goes through as group winner, while Sabalenka and Elina Svitolina meet on Friday for the other semi-final place. Svitolina kept her hopes alive by beating Karolina Muchova 3-6 6-2 6-2 after a medical timeout for a right hip injury. At the Stockholm Open, Cameron Norrie lost 7-5 6-3 to Taylor Fritz, and Holger Rune reached the quarter-finals a year after rupturing his Achilles at the event.

The 19-year-old Russian went on to deliver a statement 6-4 6-0 victory over four-time major singles winner Sabalenka. "I will be honest, I feel like Aryna did not have the best day," Andreeva told Sky Sports.

Racket.title: Give Me the Ball! review – tennis trailblazer Billie Jean King is ferocious force for equality
Racket.summary: Sparky and engaging documentary about the ‘battle of the sexes’ player, who fought her whole career to ensure the women’s game got the respect it deserved After the engaging Evert and Navratilova documentary Chris and Martina: The Final Set comes this watchable and engaging documentary portrait of Billie Jean King. It includes sparky talking-head contributions from the woman herself, in her vivid red glasses, one of many sets that she apparently carries in a separate accessory case – perhaps the influence of her old friend Elton John. There is also, of course, ample (if familiar) archive footage of her amazing climb to greatness and pop-cultural political importance. And as always with tennis documentaries, it is the British viewers, not the Americans, who can appreciate the unmistakable BBC-commentating voice of Dan Maskell. King (née Moffitt) was a ferocious force in women’s tennis from the 60s onwards and a vehement but polite advocate for equal rights on prize money. The women’s game was equally skilful, though not possessed of the same brutal brawn-power, and sold as many stadium seats. King sensationally helped to launch the Virginia Slims women’s tour – one of the great commercial revolutions in US sports, and had to work hard on promotion and sponsorship at the same time as simply training and playing. And while all this was happening, she had to come to terms with her gay sexuality, while married to the poignantly devoted Larry King, who is a gallantly supportive interviewee here. Racket.summary: Errani, Paolini first to reach FAGE WTA Finals doubles semis; Townsend, Siniakova stay alive WTA Tennis
bullets: Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini became the first doubles team to reach the semi-finals of the FAGE WTA Finals in Indian Wells, beating fourth seeds Cristina Bucsa and Nicole Melichar-Martinez 3-6, 6-2, 10-7 in 1 hour, 29 minutes. The eighth seeds, who rallied from a set down, had already beaten Taylor Townsend and Katerina Siniakova in their opening match on Sunday. They secured first place in Group 2 with a match to spare.

It is the first time in three WTA Finals appearances that the Italians have progressed beyond the group stage. Second seeds Townsend and Siniakova beat Ellen Perez and Demi Schuurs 7-6 (2), 6-3 to stay alive, and they will face Bucsa and Melichar-Martinez on Thursday for the second semi-final place. Perez and Schuurs have been eliminated.
Racket.copy:
Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini were the last doubles team to qualify for the FAGE WTA Finals, but the Italians became the first to secure a semifinal berth with their second consecutive Group 2 victory on Tuesday night in Indian Wells.

Second seeds Taylor Townsend and Katerina Siniakova also won Tuesday to keep their semifinal hopes alive at the season-ending tournament. In the final match of the day, eighth seeds Errani and Paolini rallied from a set down to defeat fourth seeds Cristina Bucsa and Nicole Melichar-Martinez 3-6, 6-2, 10-7 in 1 hour, 29 minutes.

bullets: Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova beat Coco Gauff 6-3 6-3 to become the first player to reach the last four of the WTA Finals, on her tournament debut. The 21-year-old world number eight broke Gauff's serve four times in the first set, committed only one unforced error in the second and sealed victory with an ace.

It was Noskova's sixth top-10 win of the season; she won her maiden Grand Slam at Wimbledon in July. Gauff won only six of 24 points behind her second serve and can still qualify for the semi-finals, as can Jessica Pegula. Racket.title: Zheng Qinwen becomes first home player to win China Open
Racket.summary: Zheng Qinwen becomes first home player to win China Open VnExpress International
bullets: Zheng Qinwen became the first Chinese player to win the China Open since its inception in 2004, beating fifth-ranked Mirra Andreeva in the Beijing final. The 24-year-old Olympic champion, a wildcard ranked 54th after elbow surgery in 2025, saved three set points in the second set to level at 5-5, won every point after that and sealed victory with an ace on her first match point.

It was Zheng's first title since beating Sofia Kenin in Tokyo in October 2024 and her first at WTA 1000 level. Having struggled with form and fitness since her surgery, the former world number four broke in the ninth game of the second set to lead 5-4. The 19-year-old Andreeva had started more consistently, and the crowd was at times disruptive. Zheng had beaten Andreeva in three sets in the 2024 China Open quarter-finals, their only previous meeting.
Racket.copy:

bullets: Jannik Sinner has confirmed he aims to return at the Australian Open in January, having not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July because of a knee injury. The 25-year-old, who has lost the world No 1 ranking to Alexander Zverev, won the Melbourne title in 2024 and 2025 and lost to Novak Djokovic in this year's semi-final. Speaking at a press conference in Milan, he said he may play a few earlier tournaments but would take recovery one step at a time.

Sinner thanked Jack Draper, Matteo Berrettini and Carlos Alcaraz for their support during his injury absence. Draper has ruled out a return before 2027. Sinner parted ways with coach Darren Cahill last week after four years, and Sweden's Magnus Norman has joined his team, with Simone Vagnozzi remaining for continuity. Sinner also congratulated Kimi Antonelli, 20, on becoming the youngest Formula 1 world champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Racket.title: Ahn Se-young aims to set badminton record with 12 wins in a season

bullets: World No. 1 Ahn Se-young beat Japan's world No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi 21-12, 15-21, 21-16 in the women's singles final of the BWF World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) in Yeosu on 8 November. It was her first Korea Open title since 2023 and avenged her loss to Yamaguchi in last year's final. It was her 11th title of the season, making her the first player to win 11 in two consecutive years.

Ahn has a 71-1 record this season and a 55-match winning streak since losing to China's Wang Zhiyi in the All England Open final in March. Susi Susanti's record of 59 consecutive wins stands from 1993 to 1994. Ahn is reportedly skipping the Kumamoto Masters and Hong Kong Open to rest her ankles and knees, with her next target the World Tour Finals in Hangzhou from 9 to 13 December, where winning the title would bring a 12th win and a 60-match streak.

Ahn Se-young (24, Samsung Life Insurance) is chasing an unprecedented 12 tournament wins in a single season in badminton history. Having already recorded 11 wins in a season for the second straight year, she has a chance to make new history at the final tournament of the year.

The 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Kumamoto Masters (Super 500) will take place in Kumamoto, Japan, from the 10th to the 15th. This is the final sprint for qualification. Although Yamaguchi has already secured a spot in the Finals, attention is on whether she can claim her second victory in her hometown. Can she achieve her second win in Kumamoto after two years? She has recently competed in major tournaments and is currently in the process of regaining her form. Carlos Alcaraz avenged his US Open defeat to Ben Shelton with a 7-6(7-5) 7-5 victory, claiming his maiden Paris Masters title in straight sets. Alcaraz edged a thrilling opening set, roaring towards the Paris crowd after clinching the tie-break. Neither player could find a breakthrough in a set lasting 65 minutes, with Shelton unable to convert any of his six break-point opportunities.

The second set looked to be taking a similar course of action until Shelton shocked Alcaraz with a break to love at 3-2, firing two aces past his opponent in the game, but Alcaraz bounced back with a break at the earliest opportunity to bring the scores back to level at 4-4.

Racket.title: How prize money and ranking points will be awarded at the 2026 WTA Finals
Racket.summary: Prize money is down from 12 months ago, but big ranking points are still on offer. The post How prize money and ranking points will be awarded at the 2026 WTA Finals appeared first on Tennis365 .
bullets: The winner of the 2026 WTA Finals in Indian Wells can earn up to 1,500 ranking points, the most available outside the four Grand Slams, after year-end world No. 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew with a viral illness. Players earn 200 points for each round-robin win, 400 for a semi-final win and 500 for the final, with no points awarded for qualifying.

The total prize money pool is $10m across singles and doubles, down 35.5% from $15.25m in Riyadh last season. Each singles player receives a $220,000 participation fee plus $230,000 per round-robin win. Semi-final winners earn a further $820,000 and the champion $1.64m, so an unbeaten champion would take home about $3.37m.
Racket.copy:
The 2026 WTA Tour season is coming to a close, but for eight singles players there is one more task at hand: the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. The tournament was dealt a significant blow on Saturday with Elena Rybakina, the year-end world No 1 and defending WTA Finals champion, forced to withdraw from the championships due to a viral illness.

However, action is still set to get underway to a strong start on Sunday, with Marta Kostyuk — Rybakina’s replacement — set to face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the opening singles match, before 2024 WTA Finals champion Coco Gauff faces Jessica Pegula later in the day.

Racket.title: Badminton star An Se-young wins Korea Open for record-tying 11th int'l title
Racket.summary: Badminton star An Se-young wins Korea Open for record-tying 11th int'l title The Korea Times
bullets: South Korea's An Se-young won the women's singles at the Yeosu Victor Korea Open on Sunday, beating Japan's Akane Yamaguchi 21-12, 15-21, 21-16 at Jinnam Stadium. The world No. 1 claimed her 11th international title of the year, tying the record set by Kento Momota in 2019 and equalled by An herself in 2025. The Korea Open is the only Korean event on the BWF World Tour.

An has won eight World Tour tournaments this year, plus gold at the Badminton Asia Championships, the BWF World Championships and the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. She has lost only once in 72 matches, to China's Wang Zhiyi in the All England Open final in March. She will now rest before the BWF World Tour Finals, which start on 9 December in Hangzhou, China.
Racket.copy:

An, world No. 1, defeated second-ranked Akane Yamaguchi of Japan 2-1 (21-12, 15-21, 21-16) in the women's singles final at Yeosu Victor Korea Open at Jinnam Stadium in Yeosu, some 320 kilometers southwest of Seoul.

The Korea Open is the only Korean event on the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour. This was An's 11th international victory of the year, tying the record first set by the men's singles player Kento Momota in 2019 and equaled by An herself in 2025.

bullets: Carlos Alcaraz reached the Paris Masters final with a 6-4 6-4 win over Casper Ruud in 86 minutes, and will face Ben Shelton in a rematch of their US Open quarter-final. The 23-year-old world number three had escaped two match points to beat Taylor Fritz in the previous round. He won 86% of points on his first serve and 11 of 13 points at the net.

Shelton, the world number four, beat Frenchman Luca van Assche 5-7 6-3 6-4 to become the first American men's singles finalist in Paris since 2017. He ended Alcaraz's US Open title defence in a five-set match that finished at 03:34 local time. Alcaraz, who returned from a four-month wrist injury layoff at that tournament, is on an eight-match winning streak after winning in Vienna last week.

Miyazaki's hope of a rematch with Ahn Se-young in the semifinals was also dashed. Ahn Se-young advanced to the final by defeating Hina Akechi (world No. 16) 2-0 (21-16, 21-12) in the semifinal on the 7th. Ahn Se-young's opponent in the final is Akane Yamaguchi.

The Canadian has soared into his first Super 500 final at the YEOSU Korea Open 2026, leaving behind a run of first-round exits at this level, yet adding another milestone to a standout season that already includes a Super 1000 title at the Indonesia Open.

The world No.7 defeated Lee Cheuk Yiu 19-21 21-15 21-12 to advance. He credited patience for helping him turn the match around after losing the first game to Lee who he described as “a really good player” with a “really good attack.”

The world No. 31 Kim Yoo-jung–Lee Yu-rim pair crushed China's Chen Pan-sutian–Luo Shu-min pair (world No. 66) 2-0 (21-17, 21-11) in the semifinals of the 2026 Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500) women's doubles at Jinnam Gymnasium in Yeosu on the 7th and advanced to the final.

Racket.title: Alcaraz beats Fritz to help Jodar reach ATP finals
Racket.summary: Carlos Alcaraz saves two match points to beat Taylor Fritz in the Paris Masters quarter-finals - a result which helped Spanish compatriot Rafael Jodar qualify for the ATP finals.
bullets: Carlos Alcaraz saved two match points to beat Taylor Fritz 6-7 (10-12) 7-5 6-3 in the Paris Masters quarter-finals. Fritz moved a break ahead in the second set, but Alcaraz broke him twice to level and dominated the decider after going 3-1 up. He will face either Casper Ruud or Nuno Borges in the semi-finals.

The result secured 20-year-old Spaniard Rafael Jodar a place at the ATP Finals, which run at Turin's Inalpi Arena from 15 to 22 November, and ended Fritz's hopes. Ben Shelton's 6-4 4-6 6-3 win over Tommy Paul sent Frances Tiafoe, 28, through, and both make their debuts. The qualifiers are Zverev, Medvedev, Cobolli, Fils, Alcaraz, Shelton, Tiafoe and Jodar. Jodar won his first ATP Tour title in Marrakech in April 2026 and reached the French Open quarter-finals.
Racket.copy:
Carlos Alcaraz saved two match points to beat Taylor Fritz in the Paris Masters quarter-finals - a result which helped Spanish compatriot Rafael Jodar qualify for the ATP Finals.

Alcaraz claimed a 6-7 (10-12) 7-5 6-3 win over Fritz which also ended the American's hopes of reaching the season-ending event in Turin, Italy. Fritz edged a tight opening set, winning the tie-break after both players had chances to take it.

Racket.copy:
Women's Tennis Association chair Valerie Camillo has apologised to Jessica Pegula and said the live-streaming of private comments to her coach about fellow player Mirra Andreeva was "regrettable and unacceptable".

American Pegula called Andreeva a "diva" in a private conversation with her coach after a practice session for the WTA Tour Finals on Wednesday. However, the comments were aired on a live stream after the WTA failed to tell players there were microphones on practice courts.

Racket.title: Arthur Fils offers injury update after appearing to struggle against Taylor Fritz in Paris

bullets: Arthur Fils said he was not injured after losing in straight sets to Taylor Fritz in the round of 16 at the Paris Masters, despite appearing to struggle during the match. He said Fritz was simply better, serving and returning more strongly, and that the match came down to two breaks. Fils has already confirmed his place at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Fils said he was too defensive at times on a very fast indoor hard court, and that he could have returned the second ball and used his forehand better. He has yet to debrief with his team. This season he won his maiden Masters title at the Cincinnati Open and also won the Barcelona Open, but he missed the Australian Open and Roland Garros, reached the second round at Wimbledon and lost in the first round of the US Open.

Racket.copy:
The coach who helped guide Jannik Sinner to five Grand Slam titles and the world number one spot is to leave the player's camp at the end of the year. Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament.

But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks. Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings.

Racket.title: Jannik Sinner: Coach Darren Cahill to leave Italian's side at end of 2026
Racket.summary: Jannik Sinner: Coach Darren Cahill to leave Italian's side at end of 2026 BBC
bullets: Darren Cahill will leave Jannik Sinner's coaching team at the end of 2026. The 61-year-old Australian joined in June 2022, when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10, and with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi helped him win five Grand Slams and spend 95 weeks as world number one. Swede Magnus Norman, long-time coach of recently retired Stan Wawrinka, will join the team next season.

Sinner, 25, has not played since winning Wimbledon for a second year in a row in July because of injury, and Alexander Zverev has recently overtaken him at the top of the rankings. He is set to return at the Six Kings Slam in Saudi Arabia next month. Cahill had planned to leave at the end of 2025 but told Sinner at Wimbledon he could stay if he won the title. Sinner said Cahill helped him grow as a player and as a person.

Racket.title: Youth Olympics: Malhan Makes History; Zhang Wins Thriller
Racket.summary: Youth Olympics: Malhan Makes History; Zhang Wins Thriller BWF
bullets: Riyan Malhan became the first player from the United Arab Emirates to win a gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games, beating top seed Mady Sow in the men's singles final in Dakar. Malhan came from behind in both games, winning five straight points to take the second after Sow led 18-16. In the women's singles, China's World Junior champion Zhang Yi Xin beat India's Tanvi Patri 26-24 in the third game.

Patri, the Asian U17 champion, won 11 of 12 points from 10-19 down in the decider, saved five match points to level at 20 and had three chances to take gold. Zhang saved each of them and then converted her own seventh match point. Malhan said he had been unfit and had a high fever before the matches. Hong Tian Yue of China and Japan's Yuzuno Watanabe won the bronze playoffs.

Golf.copy:
Legendary sports broadcaster Dan Hicks, one of the most well-known voices in golf, has died at the age of 64. The NBC Golf play-by-play announcer had been in his role since 2000 and commentated on a vast number of iconic moments within the sport such as Tiger Woods' famous 2008 US Open triumph and JJ Spun's 64-foot monster putt at Oakmont in 2025.

Hannah Storm, Hicks' wife and fellow announcer, confirmed his death in a statement on Thursday. Storm shared that Hicks had been suffering with an "acute illness" but his passing was "sudden" and unexpected. He is survived by his wife and three children.

Golf.title: McIlroy makes strong start in bid to equal Montgomerie's record
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy makes a strong start to his bid for a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title with a three under opening round at the DP World Tour Championship.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy made a strong start to his bid for a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title with a three-under-par opening round at the DP World Tour Championship. Golf.title: LPGA to update pace-of-play policy with stricter punishments
Golf.summary: The LPGA is updating its pace-of-play policy and dishing out stricter punishments in 2027 after pace flatlined during the 2026 season. The post LPGA to update pace-of-play policy with stricter punishments appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
The LPGA is updating its pace-of-play policy and dishing out stricter punishments in 2027 after pace flatlined during the 2026 season. Players were informed of the changes by the Pace of Play Committee during a Tuesday meeting at The Annika in Belleair, Florida, the LPGA’s penultimate event of the season.

The updated policy will include more fines. Previously, players who took one to five seconds over their allotted time to hit a shot were given two warnings before a fine. Now the warnings are gone and players will be fined right away. Six to 15 seconds over allotment remains a one-stroke penalty but a fine will now be included, and 16 seconds or more remains a two-stroke penalty but will also come with a fine.

It’s one of golf’s most grueling tests and it’s over for another year. For these players, Europe’s top table awaits in 2027… The DP World Tour Q School results are in. Teeing up at Infinitum in Spain this week were 156 hopefuls who would play 108 holes over six days in a bid for DP World Tour playing rights next season. This year’s chances were ever so slightly slimmer, with the number of available cards reduced from 20 to 15 plus ties. As it happened, 20 players did exactly that, so who booked their ticket for 2027?

Josele Ballester carded six rounds of 68 or better to finish on 32-under-par to top the leaderboard alongside fellow Spaniard Rocco Repetto-Taylor. Ballester, who joined the professional ranks last year to join Sergio Garcia’s Fireballs team on LIV Golf, made north of $10 million in two years on the league before it was wound down.

Golf.title: Carnoustie wins Open Championship bid, but there’s more to the story
Golf.summary: Carnoustie, one of the most difficult tests in pro golf, is set to host the Open Championship again. But what's different this time? The post Carnoustie wins Open Championship bid, but there’s more to the story appeared first on Golf .
bullets: The R&A announced on Monday that the Open Championship will return to Carnoustie Golf Links in 2029, the first time since 2018, when Francesco Molinari won and total attendance reached 172,000. Muirfield and Turnberry were passed over, with both reportedly presenting logistical issues around crowd space and transport.

Carnoustie's operations are now run by a consortium led by Max Herberstein, whose group bought the Carnoustie Golf Hotel for roughly £10m in 2023. In early 2025 it agreed with Angus Council and the charity running the courses to take over day-to-day golf operations for eight years. This year's Open at Royal Birkdale drew more than 300,000 spectators over eight days.
Golf.copy:
In 2029, the Open Championship will return to Carnoustie Golf Links, long heralded as one of the major’s most difficult venues. The decision, announced Monday by the R&A, feels like a no-brainer on its surface. Of course they’re headed back to one of the best golf courses on the planet.

But it came with secondary questions: Why go there before Muirfield? Or Turnberry? As the Open continues to grow in size, popularity and economic importance, decisions like this one are never just about revisiting an old stop on the event’s rota. Carnoustie’s placement, this time, is a much deeper conversation.

Golf.title: As LIV Golf fades away, one Jon Rahm question remains. He has a firm answer
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm is starting a new chapter of his career but one LIV Golf question keeps popping up. He has a firm answer. The post As LIV Golf fades away, one Jon Rahm question remains. He has a firm answer appeared first on Golf .
bullets: Jon Rahm has said his poor major record since joining LIV Golf was down to his own swing problems and not the tour. Speaking ahead of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai, he said people must stop blaming LIV. His comments follow LIV Golf's declaration in bankruptcy court last week that it would wind down operations, and Rahm's win in Abu Dhabi, his first outside LIV since his defection.

In three years on LIV, Rahm played 11 majors, with four top-10s and two missed cuts. In the three years before he left, he had seven top-10s in 12 majors, won two and missed no cuts. His only real chances came at the 2025 PGA Championship at Quail Hollow and the 2026 PGA at Aronimink, where Aaron Rai won. Rahm said he hopes his recent swing work will make him more consistent in majors.
Golf.copy:
In April of 2025, Jon Rahm said it was “unfair”. Rahm had been on LIV Golf for over a year and bemoaned being judged on his poor major record in 2024 rather than the overall state of his game, including his performance in LIV events.

“Consistency is something that I’ve always prided myself on. I think last year the state of my game was being unfairly judged based on how I played here and at the PGA compared to how I really played throughout the whole year,” Rahm said at Augusta National. “While I understand why, I don’t think it was the most fair state of my game. It’s something — top 10 statistics is something I’ve always prided myself on. Golf.title: LIV Golf seeks Chapter 11 protection amid planned 2027 relaunch
Golf.summary: LIV Golf seeks Chapter 11 protection amid planned 2027 relaunch Financier Worldwide
bullets: LIV Golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey, as part of a restructuring support agreement with UK private equity firm BC Partners Credit. The petition lists liabilities of $500m to $1bn and assets of $100m to $500m. The Public Investment Fund has agreed to provide $49.6m in debtor-in-possession financing during the court-supervised process, and BC Partners Credit and minority investors are expected to act as plan sponsors and provide exit financing.

The league intends to resume global team-based competition in 2027 under a revised ownership structure, subject to court approval and stakeholder support, and recent filings indicate players could hold a majority stake. The PIF said in April that it would stop funding the league after investing more than $5bn, and at least $45m is believed to be owed to players. Chief executive Scott O'Neil said the process gives the league time to pursue a transaction built around fans and a player-first ownership model.
Golf.copy:
Controversial breakaway golf league LIV Golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey as part of a restructuring agreement with UK private equity firm BC Partners that it hopes will secure the league’s future beyond 2026.

The organisation, which created significant division within professional golf following its launch in 2022, reported liabilities of between $500m and $1bn and assets of between $100m and $500m in its Chapter 11 petition.

Golf.title: Brown, 19, becomes youngest PGA winner in 95 years
Golf.summary: Teenager Blades Brown beats Ben James at the World Wide Technology Championship in Mexico to become the youngest PGA Tour tournament winner since 1938.
bullets: Nineteen-year-old Blades Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years by taking the World Wide Technology Championship in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico. He beat fellow American Ben James on the second play-off hole after a nine-under-par 63, including a birdie on the 18th, to come from seven shots behind. Both finished on 23 under, with Michael Kim third on 22 under.

At 19 years and 171 days, Brown is the youngest winner since Charles Kocsis, 18, won the 1931 Michigan Open. He is the first teenage winner since Jordan Spieth won the 2013 John Deere Classic at 19 years and 352 days. Brown turned professional at 17 and secured his PGA Tour card by finishing in the top 20 of the Korn Ferry Tour points list earlier this year. He said the magnitude of the win had not yet set in.

At 19 years and 171 days, he is the youngest PGA winner since 18-year-old Charles Kocsis won the 1931 Michigan Open, which was considered a regional event in the early years of the tour.

LIV filed for bankruptcy in September after PIF, previously a 98% stakeholder, withdrew its financial backing.

BC Partners had committed $300m to a proposed successor of up to 17 tournaments, but the plan reportedly collapsed over player financial guarantees. It believes PGA Tour schedule changes from 2028 and the DP World Tour's financial difficulties could leave room for a team-based rival. Bryson DeChambeau said he "gave everything" to keep team golf alive and will play the Nedbank Golf Challenge next month. The DP World Tour has reportedly offered him an automatic 2027 exemption, with one week to decide.
Golf.copy:
LIV Golf may not be dead just yet, according to a report. According to the Financial Times, BC Partners has quietly revived its attempts to create a successor to the breakaway tour, after abandoning its plans for a "LIV 2.0" last week.

He left the BMW PGA Championship having finished dead last, his pre-occupied by the impending arrival of his fourth child and – to a lesser extent – his exit from LIV Golf.

But in his first start since that ignominious visit to Wentworth and having left the doomed breakaway league with millions of dollars on the table, Rahm is a winner again. On debut here at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, Rahm held off Ryder Cup teammates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy to win by two strokes with an imperious final round 67 at Yas Links.

Golf.copy:
One of the nice things about being Jon Rahm is that your reputation precedes you. You don’t need to provide your credentials to earn a tee time at the local club, or explain to the restaurant that you’d prefer a private table, or justify your desire to read your own putts to your caddie. You are Jon Rahm. Your resume speaks for itself.

As it turns out, that’s also why these few months are some of the weirdest of Rahm’s career. After LIV’s collapse, Rahm is suddenly auditioning for his pro career’s future, and hoping that a series of strong performances in the middle of the international fall season can help expedite his path back to the PGA Tour. And on Saturday evening in Abu Dhabi, Rahm’s resume means a little bit less than his spot on the 54-hole leaderboard: solo first.

Golf.summary: While Rory McIlroy and others are willing to welcome LIV defectors back to the PGA Tour, not everyone has the same feeling. "Go to Q school." The post LIV Golf’s end brought harsh answers to the sport’s most pressing question appeared first on Golf .
Golf.copy:
Facing what would become golf’s biggest question, Xander Schauffele said he wasn’t sure where he stood. Jon Rahm’s attorney had just announced his client’s departure from LIV Golf, and Schauffele, one of the faces of the PGA Tour, was asked about a road back for defectors like Rahm. He didn’t divulge his feelings on the matter, but his explanation for the obstacles ahead once the LIV threat officially ended would prove prescient one month later.

“I’ve got no idea,” Schauffele said at the Baycurrent Classic last month. “There are 225 guys with Tour cards and if you sat down and interviewed all of them, you’re going to get probably three or four boxes of how guys feel. Some guys don’t care, some guys are really ticked off, some guys want them to have a huge fine, some guys would let them back tomorrow. Where I stand in those boxes, I don’t really know. I’m in the sort of, I try to mind my own business most times.”

Ryder Cup team-mates Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton reeled in Francesco Laporta to share the lead heading into the weekend at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship. Italian Laporta had led after a brilliant 62 on day one but a 70 in round two at Yas Links left the door ajar and close friends Hatton and Rahm took advantage.

Hatton carded a 65, two shots fewer than Rahm, and the pair will now both head into the weekend at 12 under alongside Laporta looking for a record sixth Rolex Series victory. Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau Dealt Great News After LIV Golf Shutdown
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau Dealt Great News After LIV Golf Shutdown Heavy.com
bullets: Bryson DeChambeau has been offered full DP World Tour playing privileges for 2027, according to The Telegraph, as LIV Golf moves towards liquidation. He qualifies under the Category 1 exemption, which covers major winners and Race to Dubai champions from the past seven years, through his 2024 US Open win at Pinehurst. He must submit his membership application by 14 November and has not confirmed whether he will accept.

LIV's board confirmed an orderly wind-down after the league failed to secure investment for its LIV 2.0 format. BC Partners had considered investing $300m but withdrew after failing to secure commitments from leading players. A top-10 finish on the 2027 Race to Dubai could help DeChambeau regain a PGA Tour card for 2028, though he may face a one-year suspension, as Jon Rahm expects to. Rahm is expected to play the DP World Tour in 2027, with Hatton and Garcia expected to return to Europe.
Golf.copy:
Bryson DeChambeau faces an important decision about his professional golf future after the collapse of LIV Golf. The American has been one of the breakaway league’s biggest names since joining in 2022. His two US Open victories and growing popularity have kept him among the sport’s most recognizable players.

After making a slice of personal history in Abu Dhabi, Rory McIlroy reflected on the news of LIV Golf’s demise. Not in 21 years and 1,014 rounds on the DP World Tour had Rory McIlroy ever made 11 birdies in a competitive round. But just 24 hours after accepting a two-shot penalty which seemed a significant blow to his hopes of winning a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai, McIlroy conjured another magical personal record as he surged into contention at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship.

McIlroy’s 9-under par 63 lit up the second round at Yas Links, a blitz that included seven birdies on the back nine. It all came after taking an unplayable and making bogey on the first, as well as the rules incident that threatened to spoil a solid start to his tournament.

Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy recovers from the setback of being penalised two shots in his opening round at the Abu Dhabi Championship by firing 11 birdies in a nine-under-par 63 in round two on Friday.
bullets: Rory McIlroy carded a nine-under-par 63 in the second round of the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links, making 11 birdies to reach 11 under overall and move within one shot of the lead. Spain's Jon Rahm, England's Tyrrell Hatton and Italy's Francesco Laporta share the lead at 12 under, while McIlroy sits in a four-strong group alongside Sam Bairstow, Matthew Jordan and Adrian Meronk.

McIlroy had finished the first round two under par, eight shots off the lead, after a two-shot penalty for improving his lie on the 12th hole. He said he had "made peace" with the ruling and played with a clear conscience. He is chasing a fifth consecutive Race to Dubai title and a record-equalling eighth overall, level with Colin Montgomerie. The top 50 in the rankings progress to next week's season-ending DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.
Golf.copy:
Rory McIlroy posted 11 birdies in a nine-under-par second-round 63 at the Abu Dhabi Championship to move within one shot of the lead. The 37-year-old put the setback of the two-shot penalty he received on Thursday behind him as he completed the best round of the day to reach 11 under overall.

Spain's Jon Rahm, England's Tyrell Hatton and Italy's Francesco Laporta share the lead at 12 under, while McIlroy is part of a four-strong group that includes the English duo of Sam Bairstow and Matthew Jordan, plus Poland's Adrian Meronk.

bullets: Rory McIlroy's Boston Common Golf and Tiger Woods' Jupiter Links Golf Club will both play in an opening-night double-header on 27 December at the SoFi Center, launching an expanded third season of the TGL presented by SoFi. McIlroy's side, who signed Shane Lowry in the off-season, face new team Motor City Golf Club, featuring Brooks Koepka and Jackson Koivun. Woods' team meet defending champions Los Angeles Golf Club in a rematch of last year's SoFi Cup Finals.

The league grows to seven teams of five players. Woods, 50, held a non-playing role in 2026 because of injury and made one appearance in the season finale, but former team-mate Kevin Kisner said Woods plans to play a full schedule. Each team plays four group fixtures, the semi-finals begin the week of 15 March, and the best-of-three Finals Series runs on 22 and 23 March. The 35 players have won 38 majors between them.
Golf.copy:

Season three launches on December 27 at the SoFi Center, with Woods and McIlroy returning as at least 12 new PGA Tour players joining TGL ahead of the 2027 season. - When will Tiger Woods play next and return to PGA Tour?

Golf.title: Iconic PGA Tour Venue To Drop Off Schedule After 80 Years
Golf.summary: Colonial Country Club has reportedly lost out on hosting a Championship Series event so will drop off the 2028 PGA Tour schedule for the first time in 80 years
bullets: Colonial Country Club in Fort Worth, Texas, host of the Charles Schwab Challenge and the longest-running venue on the PGA Tour schedule outside the majors, is reportedly set to lose its place in 2027 after 80 years. Golfweek reports the tournament will not make the new PGA Tour Championship Series in 2028, as only one Championship Series event will be staged in the Dallas-Fort Worth area and the CJ Cup Byron Nelson sponsors have made a stronger bid.

Colonial officials are reported to be unwilling to host a second-tier Challenger Series event and may instead look to stage the season-ending Charles Schwab Cup Championship on PGA Tour Champions. The Sony Open in Hawaii has already made that switch, and PGA Tour Champions president Miller Brady says other courses have been in touch. Officials at Colonial and Charles Schwab are reportedly unhappy, though some hope of a late reprieve remains.
Golf.copy:
The iconic Colonial Country Club is the longest running host on the PGA Tour schedule, but 2027 will reportedly bring that 80-year streak to an end. The esteemed course in Fort Worth, Texas, hosts the Charles Schwab Challenge but Golfweek reports that the tournament will not be making it onto the new PGA Tour Championship Series in 2028.

Citing inside sources, the report states only one Championship Series event will be staged in the Dallas-Fort Worth area and the CJ Cup Byron Nelson sponsors have made a greater bid.
